scope: Static inspection of frozen run01 uninstrumented P=false reducer machine code; no rebuild, job or performance measurement.

normalizations: PlannedReducer call plus plan tile context

findings.claim: ExactI duplicate decode is NOT eliminated by compiler CSE
findings.qualified: One matched pair of 128-wide source rows per iteration; arithmetic count is independent of optional prefetch branches.

findings.claim: Exact kernels have no per-edge head-value matching
findings.explanation: Their three scalar comparisons test loop exit and two row-scope prefetch boundaries, never current source-index equality/order. Dynamic I/S retain head comparisons in listed regions. A precomputed mask bit is tested once per pair window outside these loops.

findings.claim: Current CSR index requests in ExactS decrease by one per exact edge pair, while both next-index paths remain
findings.qualified: Logical current requests are E-c only for exact S; next requests still depend on each row scope. These are not cache/DRAM byte measurements.

findings.claim: No vector accumulator stack spills found in reviewed uninstrumented reducer symbols
findings.qualified: The functions use rsp for stack frame and scalar metadata; rbp is repurposed as a data pointer. Explicit partial/packed accesses through pointer registers are algorithmic state, not spills. Instrumented P=true code is outside this no-spill claim.

findings.claim: Scalar fallback arithmetic is preserved but full functions differ
findings.qualified: MODE0 register allocation and surrounding pair/window control differ from MODE3/4, so identical source helper does not imply identical total timing. Exact paths include mask metadata and branch costs.

findings.claim: ExactS has additional scalar metadata reloads in this register allocation
findings.explanation: Second-row prefetch reloads the bases pointer from rsp+0x20 and then its row base. This remains in measured code and partly offsets deleted current-index/decode work.
